task.description: Gate ELIXIR-DEV's ISS-0519 fix (entity_definitions versioning safety: deterministic get_definition_by_name/2, new get_active_definition_by_name/2 routed through Activation.resolve/3, transactional demote-then-promote activate_definition/4, and the new partial-unique-index migration with data remediation) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8.

result.note:
Scope test: applies (tenant-scoped table entity_definitions, a new migration, and a lookup-by-name/version handler are all touched). Gated per-invariant: INV-1 (tenant isolation on the migration/schema) APPLIES and PASSES -- the migration is correctly guarded by `if prefix() do ... end` (matching 20260906000001_create_entity_definitions.exs's own precedent), all identifiers interpolated into the raw SQL (schema) come from Ecto.Migration's own trusted prefix(), never caller/tenant input, and the remediation UPDATE/CREATE INDEX both execute strictly inside that one tenant's schema -- confirmed no cross-schema reference anywhere in the file. Registered correctly in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (verified at tenant_provisioning.ex:500). INV-4 (secrets) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no secret/config/token resolution touched. INV-7 (no SQL injection) APPLIES and PASSES -- the migration's execute/2 call interpolates only the trusted `schema` variable (via #{schema}), no caller-controlled name/id/tenant value is interpolated into SQL text anywhere in the diff; all application-code queries (definitions.ex, records.ex) use parameterized Ecto.Query pin syntax throughout, no string-built queries. INV-8 (no unhandled crash on tenant-reachable input) APPLIES and PASSES -- this is literally what the fix closes: get_definition_by_name/2 no longer raises Ecto.MultipleResultsError (order_by+limit:1 added), get_active_definition_by_name/2 never raises on a resolve/3 not-found or an orphaned artifact_version_id (returns {:error, :not_found} in both cases), activate_definition/4's new transactional promote/demote path returns a typed {:error, {:persistence, changeset}} rather than raising on a concurrent constraint conflict. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 (S4/S5-stage invariants) correctly assessed NOT-APPLICABLE -- no auth/authorization-boundary or cross-service-token code touched by this diff.

Independent verification performed beyond trusting the handoff's claims: (1) Read get_active_definition_by_name/2 (definitions.ex) directly -- confirmed its entity_definitions lookup filters on BOTH e.tenant_id == ^tenant_id (derived from prefix via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, never caller-supplied) AND e.artifact_version_id == ^version_id, where version_id is read verbatim off the %Repository.ArtifactVersion{} struct returned by Activation.resolve/3's own {:ok, ...} branch -- never a separately-trusted or caller-influenced value, so the two lookups are genuinely correlated and cannot be tricked into crossing tenants or names. (2) Read Activation.resolve/3 (activation.ex:160-177) -- confirms its own tenant scoping relies on schema-per-tenant Repo prefix isolation (same established belt-and-suspenders convention as list_definitions/2), consistent with every other Decision-B table in this codebase; not a new gap introduced by this fix. (3) Traced the remediation UPDATE's ROW_NUMBER()/PARTITION BY (tenant_id, name) logic against Activation.resolve/3's authoritative active_version_id pointer semantics: ranking by MAX(artifact_activation_history.activated_at) per (artifact_kind='entity', artifact_name, new_version_id=ed.artifact_version_id), falling back to ed.inserted_at only for a row with zero matching history (an edge case the migration's own comment documents as 'should not occur under the current data model'), correctly identifies the same row Activation.resolve/3 would call authoritative, since the activation pointer's active_version_id is by construction the version_id of the most recently completed activate_group call for that name. On a schema with exactly one active row per name (the expected/observed state in every test-provisioned schema this session), rn=1 for that row and the UPDATE's WHERE id IN (...rn>1...) matches zero rows -- confirmed genuinely idempotent/no-op there, not merely claimed so. (4) Confirmed the migration's own up/down split (data-mutating up/0, index-drop-only down/0 that explicitly does not attempt to reverse the remediation) follows the cited 20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs precedent's own convention (use up/down not change/0 for a genuinely irreversible data-dependent step, document why down/0 is a partial/no-op reversal, not a lie about reversibility) -- read that precedent file directly and confirmed the parallel holds. (5) Traced promote_and_demote_siblings/2 (definitions.ex:427-449): demote (Ecto.Multi.update_all) and promote (Ecto.Multi.update) both run inside one Repo.transaction/1 -- confirmed atomic (no way to observe only one half applied), and confirmed the demote-before-promote statement ordering inside that transaction matches the moduledoc's own stated invariant (never transiently violates the new partial unique index at any statement boundary within a single activation). For the cross-request concurrent-activation case, confirmed serialization comes from two independent, stacked mechanisms and verified both are real, not just asserted: (a) Activation.activate_group/5's own FOR UPDATE row lock on the artifact_activations row for (tenant_id, artifact_kind, artifact_name) -- read activation.ex directly, confirmed this runs and commits strictly before promote_and_demote_siblings/2 is ever invoked, so two concurrent activate_definition/4 calls for the same name are already fully ordered before either reaches the entity_definitions-side transaction; (b) even without that upstream lock, the new partial unique index is a real Postgres-enforced backstop -- a second transaction's promote step attempting to set status=active while another row is already committed active for the same (tenant_id, name) will block on the index's implicit row-insertion lock and then fail with a unique-constraint violation on commit/statement execution, which EntityDefinition.changeset/2's new unique_constraint(:status, name: :entity_definitions_tenant_name_active_idx) correctly translates into a typed changeset error (confirmed the constraint name in entity_definition.ex matches the migration's index name exactly, char-for-char). No route or controller file appears anywhere in `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (verified directly) -- no auth/route gap possible from this diff.

One non-blocking observation (not a security defect, does not gate this review): if Activation.activate_group/5 succeeds but the immediately-following entity_definitions demote/promote transaction subsequently fails (e.g. loses a same-name concurrent-activation race against the partial unique index), the caller receives {:error, {:persistence, changeset}} even though the activation pointer itself (the actually-authoritative artifact_activations row) already moved -- a residual denormalization-column inconsistency, not a tenant-isolation or data-integrity defect, since get_active_definition_by_name/2's own query never filters on entity_definitions.status and therefore stays correct regardless of this edge case. Flagging forward for REVIEWER/ELIXIR-DEV's awareness, not blocking this gate.

Commands run directly by SECURITY-REVIEWER, real output: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, zero warnings/errors. `mix test test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs` -- 46 passed, 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/entities/` -- 103 passed, 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/repository/` -- 56 passed, 0 failures (no stale tenant_template rebuild was needed this run -- template was already current from ELIXIR-DEV's own prior rebuild in this session).
